name: Panasonic eneloop AA Rechargeable Batteries with BQ-CC17 Charger
summary: Four standard white AA NiMH cells and a BQ-CC17 AC charger for compatible battery-powered equipment. Charge a spare set before an outage; check device voltage and chemistry requirements.
description: Small emergency devices need a battery plan as much as larger power stations do. This AA starter kit pairs four standard eneloop rechargeable cells with the independently controlled BQ-CC17 charger. Keep an appropriately charged spare set for equipment whose instructions accept 1.2 V NiMH AA cells. The wall-powered charger needs a suitable AC supply, so it cannot replenish batteries by itself during a blackout. AA cells are physically different from AAA cells; neither format nor an illustrated device establishes compatibility. The manufacturer kit contains four cells and one charger, despite extra decorative cells in the artwork.

specs.label: Kit
specs.value: Four standard white AA eneloop NiMH cells and one BQ-CC17 charger; K-KJ17MCA4BA

specs.label: Capacity
specs.value: Up to 2000 mAh / minimum 1900 mAh; manufacturer capacity convention, not measured runtime

specs.label: Charger
specs.value: BQ-CC17, individually controlled slots for 1–4 compatible AA/AAA eneloop NiMH cells

specs.label: AC input
specs.value: 100–240 V AC; regional plug varies. Not a USB or solar-input charger.

specs.label: Charge
specs.value: About 7 hours for 1–4 AA cells in the 1900–2000 mAh band at room temperature; temperature and cell condition affect time

specs.label: Cycles
specs.value: Up to 2100 under IEC 61951-2:2011 (7.5.1.3); 600 under IEC 61951-2:2017 (7.5.1.4). Usage conditions affect life.

pros: Four rechargeable AA cells form one clearly defined starter set for compatible equipment.
Independent slot control lets the BQ-CC17 charge one to four compatible AA or AAA cells.
cons: Use only in devices whose instructions accept AA 1.2 V NiMH cells; size alone is insufficient.
The BQ-CC17 needs AC power and takes about 7 hours in the documented capacity band; it is not an instant outage recharge source.
Advertised capacity and cycle counts are conditional manufacturer figures, not guaranteed device runtime or service life.
useCases: Prepare labelled AA spare sets for a radio or light only after its instructions confirm 1.2 V NiMH compatibility.
Recharge compatible cells before forecast outages and include a separate plan for extended loss of AC power.

safetyNotes: Charge only compatible rechargeable NiMH cells in the BQ-CC17. Do not charge alkaline, primary lithium or lithium-ion cells. Follow polarity markings and the supplied instructions.
Keep the charger dry, ventilated and on an appropriate indoor AC supply. Inspect cells and charger for damage; discontinue use if damaged or abnormal.
Store spare cells with protected terminals away from loose metal. Follow device instructions for matched cells and do not mix damaged, depleted or incompatible cells.
AA and AAA are different sizes. Neither kit establishes compatibility with ORIA, a particular radio or an emergency light; check its voltage and chemistry requirements.
